directAnswer: You can find your router's IP address by checking your device's network settings or using the command prompt/terminal.
summary: This guide provides methods to locate your router's IP address on different platforms.

sections.heading: Using Network Settings
sections.body: On most devices, you can find your router's IP address in the network settings. This method varies slightly between operating systems.

sections.heading: Using Command Line
sections.body: You can also use command line tools to find your router's IP address, which is particularly useful for advanced users.

steps.title: Windows
steps.detail: Open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. Look for 'Default Gateway' under your network connection.

steps.title: macOS
steps.detail: Go to System Preferences > Network, select your active connection, and click 'Advanced'. The router's IP will be listed under the 'TCP/IP' tab.

steps.title: Linux
steps.detail: Open Terminal and type 'ip route | grep default'. The router's IP address will be shown after 'default via'.

steps.title: iOS
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Wi-Fi, tap the information icon (i) next to your connected network, and find the router's IP address.

steps.title: Android
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi, tap on your connected network, and look for the router's IP address.

faqs.question: What if I can't find my router's IP address?
faqs.answer: Ensure you are connected to the network and check if the router is powered on. If issues persist, refer to your router's manual.

faqs.question: Can my router's IP address change?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your router is set to obtain an IP address automatically from your Internet Service Provider, it may change periodically.

faqs.question: What is the default IP address for most routers?
faqs.answer: Common default IP addresses include 192.168.1.1 and 192.168.0.1, but this can vary by manufacturer.

caveats: The steps may vary slightly depending on the version of the operating system.
